Figure 2:Paradigms for self-supervised latent-action learning.Existing methods learn latent actions
(a) from scratch[8,85,20],
(b) on frozen visual features[9,21],
(c) with a pretrained video generator as the FDM only[62,76],
or (d) with an external video prior as auxiliary supervision[35].Oursrepurposes one pretrained video DiT as both the IDM and the FDM.
Figure 3:Action-aware response in a pretrained video DiT.Cross-attention follows the active hands and manipulated regions as the interaction changes.

Figure 5:Overview of O2LaF.Two independently adapted video DiTs share a pretrained prior:
the IDM infers latent actions, while the FDM predicts their
visual consequences.
Both employ frame-causal attention and role-specific
noise sampling, with end-to-end training through latent actions.

Figure 7:Zero-shot cross-context camera navigation.O2LaF better reproduces reference camera and agent
action while preserving the target scene.

Figure 8:Zero-shot cross-embodiment manipulationO2LaF better preserves object-directed motion
while adapting to the target embodiment and visual context.

Figure 9:Role-specific noise levels.IDM linear probing across
a5×55\times 5grid of IDM and FDM flow times.
The non-monotonic trends reveal distinct preferred
noise configurations across motion domains.

Figure 10:Cross-context action transfer with IDM priors.V-JEPA2 exhibits source-appearance leakage,
whereas video DiT better preserves target appearance.

Figure 11:Where does the pairwise action query attend?For transitionxt→xt+1x_{t}\!\rightarrow x_{t+1}, action queryqtq_{t}jointly attends
to spatial video tokens in both endpoint frames.

Figure 12:The FDM as a policy verifier on a GR-1 humanoid.Each case shows one trajectory in the physics simulator rebuilt from a single photo (top), the same motion with objects removed, from which latent actions are extracted (middle), and the FDM rollout from the real photo (bottom).
